notes.title: Demo Update 1.1 - new UI and important fixes
notes.content:
Hello everyone

We keep working on the project and it is getting closer and closer to completion. We have some big news coming up soon. Our plans to release an Extended Free Demo (including Chapters 1 and 2) in a few months remain unchanged. Today, though, we update the current Demo (Chapter 1) to implement new UI elements. It is still a work in progress and we plan to implement tutorial hints and a few other key elements in future updates. 

Changelog:

1) Major change - UI overhaul. It now has a much better visual representation of various parameters. It is still a work in progress, so new elements will be added further. 
2) Major change - Reworked the resolutions support system. It helped us fix some issues we had previously. 
3) Changes to the saves system - work in progress. 
4) The game is now captured by OBS without issues.
5) Fixed some visual issues in Chapter 1 art assets. 

Note! The old save files no longer work as intended. We are sorry for the inconvenience. We are still working on the game and it requires making some big changes to it. This can still happen until we release the Extended Demo - at that point, we will finalize the save files system and will support all subsequent game versions without issues with save files - so you will be able to use your saves from future versions of the Demo and Extended Demo to keep playing from where you left once the full game is released. 

Stay tuned for future updates and free Extended Demo release to be announced soon.

Starni Games team

notes.title: Meet the characters: Robert Everett
notes.content:
Robert Everett is one of the main characters in Robot’s Fate: Alice. Robert is among the first people you meet in the game, as he is the designated owner of CCM-924209, also known as Alice. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45140388/4f0bc61948021307cebe8bd6f3ddff24f87c607e.jpg[/img]

Robert Everett is no stranger to dealing with robots. As an MIT graduate in robotics and current CTO of RobotX, the largest seller of robots and AI technologies at the start of the story, Robert has always been interested in science and technology. What started as a childhood hobby of taking toys to pieces and assembling them back again, consuming sci-fi stories in all shapes and forms, and dreaming big led to a remarkable career in robotics. Robert has been working in RobotX for more than a decade now and is responsible for the company’s renaissance after the infamous Ellsworth Incident. Not only did his new revolutionary neuromatrices save RobotX from bankruptcy, but they also started a new era of AI companionship changing the world forever.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45140388/4ec29df37be70c2d0a70b573758a49d2a11fc92e.jpg[/img]

In a way, he is the father of Alice (and countless other robots). It rhymes well with how Robert behaves. Unlike many people who tend to ignore robots and never treat them as living beings, Robert takes his time to explain anything Alice might ask and allows her to feel like a family member.

In his free time from work, Robert geeks out by watching movies, playing video games, and tinkering in his workshop, which he may or may not use as an excuse to smoke away from his wife’s accusatory look. His workshop encapsulates Robert’s heart and soul. His passion fueled by tobacco and the blackest coffee is reflected by dozens of instruments scattered across the room, unfinished projects waiting for another quick five minutes of his busy time, loose ends queueing to get his attention, and humble beginnings always at the threshold, always piquing his interest and distracting from finishing the previous ones. It’s a constant race against time with Robert trying desperately to handle all his activities. His working space personifies his creativity, both in much disarray and disorder.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45140388/55411d55ed2f65cd7a10796938dfea83d4e5b9d0.jpg[/img]

Anyway, it is hard to be a good father, RobotX’s employed genius, and non-stop creator of gadgets when there are only twenty-four hours in a day! Can we all admit that he’s doing rather well?

Check Robot’s Fate: Alice to meet Robert and many more interesting characters while surviving as a “young” robot with a newly emerging sentience.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3091030/Robots_Fate_Alice/

notes.title: Early Demo reception and feedback. What comes next?
notes.content:
Hello

The Demo was out for a few months and we are extremely thankful to everyone who played it, especially those who took their time to fill in the feedback form that could be found in the game. Now, we would like to share some key insights that we found through the feedback form. We would also provide an even more detailed report to everyone who subscribed to the Robot’s Fate: Alice newsletter in a week. 

[b]Overall impression[/b]

The overall feedback is quite positive and the most important thing for us is that most of the players are really interested in the story’s continuation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45140388/d3e0329dfc9a3f9cccf0df32bb7010fd34da4672.png[/img]

We asked a few questions to see what the general impression is and how much do you enjoy the narrative of the game - as it is something that holds everything else together. Here is what we found:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45140388/bdc9e690d1b5b86a66b2172ac53564d2ba5e1831.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45140388/e50e7aae53d0dc46d1d479602a7a7c3bba633a69.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45140388/020359be7b8d8b698beb91e58c83275ce1a6a367.png[/img]

[b]Key takeaways[/b]

Of course, there were more questions and answers and you can learn all of that in the full report we will share via email with the newsletter subscribers.
There were some issues we managed to identify - for example, the lack of clarity as to how the Neural capacity works, what are conditional events and what are the Traits. 
The key question is - what do we do with this feedback? 

Here are a few key things we decided to make our top priority:
1) Finalize the UI and make it more user-friendly
2) Add special hints and a help button that would help everyone better understand how the game works and learn it in no time. 
3) Solve some technical issues that we found thanks to your feedback (For example we already reworked the way the screen resolutions are handled)
4) Fix a few issues that were overlooked in the art assets of the game to further increase its quality.

[b]Further plans[/b]

Previously, we planned to deliver the “expanded Demo” with Chapters 1 and 2 prior to the full home release - and that plan remains unchanged, At the same time seeing your feedback, we think that we would update the current Ddemo first with some changes and improvements and only after that release the expanded Demo. We are really looking forward to seeing your feedback materialize and make the game better. 

Thank you all for playing Robot’s Fate: Alice and sharing your feedback! You did your part - and now it is up to us to produce improvements based on your input. 

Have a great day everyone and see you in the next Dev update. 

Starni Games team

notes.title: Independence Day of Ukraine 2024 - Ukrainian Games Festival
notes.content:
Hello

It is Oleksandr from Starni Games, and our entire team is extremely excited to share with you the joyous moment in the middle of the third year of brutal war raging in our country. It is the third Independence Day of Ukraine celebrated after the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine, and that in itself is an achievement. We sincerely hope that in one year this occasion will be more peaceful and the war will be over on good terms for Ukraine. 

[h3]Today, we want to share with you how our team adapted to the ongoing war, as well as unveil some of our plans for the future. [/h3]

When the war started back in February 2022, we spent the first few months adapting to the new reality:
[list]
[*] Looking for bomb shelters, making reserves of food and water supplies
[*] Living in the city with the enemy at its doorstep. (One advanced Russian group's APC was eliminated next to my colleagues' house in the middle of the city during the chaotic first few days.)
[*] One of our team was trapped in Bucha occupied by Russian forces and was hiding with his family in a garage basement for a week before evacuating to safety via road where some civilian cars were shot to bits later on the same day. 
[*] Taking PC from office to home to be able to work. This seemingly simple action looked like a special ops operation - as public transport was unavailable and the whole city in curfew with barricades and checkpoints all across the city. 
[*] Being forced to go to a bomb shelter 10 or more times a day - turning your whole day and night into the walk to and from a shelter (or sleeping on some mats inside).
[*] Catching some scum that wanted to exploit the situation or just was drunk and not in their right mind (in my house neighbors caught a guy trying to steal a bicycle). There were some photos of wanna-be looters tied to a tree with tape by the locals - to await the arrival of the police who had more urgent matters to attend to with the Russian troops just a few kilometers from the city. The guy we caught was saved from this fate by his mom coming over from nearby houses and “crying murder”. However, the next day we saw a photo of the very same guy tied to a tree, so his adventures did not stop at our place. 
[*] Trying to make sense of the literal flood of information, misinformation, wild rumors, and made-up stories from all around. (That was one of the things that inspired us to be very cautious when working on Ukraine War Stories not to provide any unconfirmed information - and it paid off, as some of the claims we discarded as dubious and unconfirmed (even though they were made by some officials) were later debunked as false claims and there was a scandal. We avoided being mixed up in that and provided accurate accounts.)
[*] Going to the outskirts of the city 3 km from the Rissian positions to where my colleague lived to pick him up and invite him to live at my apartment for a while - as he lived in literally the outermost house in Kyiv - the closest to the frontline positions. 
[*] Eagerly awaiting good news and sharing every new video or crucial report.
[/list]

In April 2022 Russian troops were forced to retreat from the Kyiv region, and most people on the team who left the city have returned (around 50% of the team moved from Kyiv, while 50% remained in the city during the first month). Also, we more or less adapted to the situation and returned to remote work. 

In June 2022 we returned to office work and moved to a bigger office in July 2022 as the price or rental dropped due to obvious reasons - half of the city left, and we planned to hire a few more people, with our old office already being overcrowded. 

In July 2022 the buildings on the way to our office and the subway station we use were hit by Russian missiles, fortunately, none on the team was affected. The subway suffered only mild damage, so was quickly reopened. Overall, from July 2022 to October 2022 we worked more or less normally (the only issue was that public transport would not always work due to air alerts) We produced Ukraine War Stories from May to October 2022.

Later in October 2022, Russia started targeting the power grind much more. It resulted in regular power outages and scheduled power supply. We had to switch to remote work - as there was little sense in sitting in an office without power for 4-5 hours. It was hard due to different parts of the city having different “shifts” of when they had power, so different people would work at different times and to share/update the work we had to have power at the same time as the office (or partially overlap). 

In December 2022 we finally managed to install a power generator in the office and returned to office work, switching between the central power and generator.

In May 2022 the power outages stopped and we could work normally without using our generator, until spring 2024, when Russians again started prioritizing power supply infrastructure and destroyed many of Ukraine’s power plants and other facilities. 

From spring 2024 to now there have been scheduled power outages, but now we are better prepared - we improved our power infrastructure in the office - so it now switches to batteries seamlessly when the power is out and when batteries are at 50% - the generator starts automatically to recharge them (they are also recharged by normal power supply when it is back up). Also, if anyone works from home there was time to buy some large batteries for households to store some energy for when the power is out. Not enough to cook, but enough to recharge a laptop and some other stuff. 

So, now we [i]stopped caring about air alerts[/i] (maybe 3-6 months into the war), we heard enough explosions to treat them as “weather” if they are not really close. We adapted our work to be able to do our job efficiently despite power outages internet issues and other problems that might arise. We keep going, and Ukraine keeps going. 

[b]Today, the Independence Day of Ukraine feels so much more important than before the war - as now our country truly paid a horrible price for its independence and has truly become independent. (Despite what some say about the foreign help, it does not make Ukraine someone’s puppet - we just want to survive and come out stronger than ever - so that we can live peacefully after the war.)[/b]

Also, to celebrate this year's Independence Day we invite you to play our fully free (charity) game we developed and released back in 2022 about civilians in the first few weeks of the Russian invasion:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1985510/Ukraine_War_Stories/

You can see a lot of similarities between how the Ukraine War Stories and Robot’s Fate: Alice are designed. That is because back in 2021 we already were doing some preproduction on Robot’s Fate: Alice, and used some of that tools and knowledge to design and develop Ukraine War Stories faster. Then we used the knowledge we gained while working on Ukraine War Stories to improve the further development of Robot’s Fate: Alice. 

You could also check out Headquarters: World War II - our latest release (April 2024) mostly developed during and despite the war (it is really ironic to make a game about World War II during an actual war):

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1840800/Headquarters_World_War_II/

Also, you can have a look at our Strategic Mind series - it's now heavily discounted:

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/16499/Strategic_Mind_Complete_Collection/

And, of course, visit the Ukrainian Games Festival on Steam to browse over 450 games created by Ukrainian devs and celebrate this wonderful day with us all:

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/ukrainiangames2024]VISIT FESTIVAL ON STEAM
[/url]
Right now, we are focused on supporting the Headquarters: World War II and working on further DLCs for it, including the already announced - Market Garden, which will be released in September 2024. We also plan to release Robot’s Fate: Alice next year, our first large-scale text-based game that will show us whether there is a way for us to move forward with this genre. 

[b]We also encourage you to play the Robot’s Fate: Alice Demo and let us know your thoughts on it via the in-game feedback form. We will share all the feedback we gathered with you soon. [/b]

Support Ukraine!

[i]With Best Regards from Kyiv
Oleksandr the the Starni Games team[/i]

notes.title: Announcing Robot’s Fate: Alice
notes.content:
[h2]Greetings, fellow human beings![/h2]

We’re thrilled to announce [b][i]Robot's Fate: Alice[/i][/b], a fresh and engaging text-based RPG by Starni Games. It is a story about our future and how advanced AI will change it. To better understand the AI and its interaction with humans, we placed ourselves in the boots of an AI-powered Child Companion robot - Alice. 

We are eager to share with you the Robot’s Fate: Alice announcement trailer:

[previewyoutube=QxygnE6X2RA;full][/previewyoutube]

Robot's Fate: Alice dives deep into thought-provoking themes about AI and humanity. Your decisions will explore the role of self-learning AI in society, the ethical treatment of robots, and the differences between AI and humans.

[h3]What's inside:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Over[b] 220 000 words[/b] of immersive narrative in 5 chapters
[*] Over [b]150 meaningful choices [/b]to make
[*] The branching storyline to explore
[*] [b]Thousands [/b]of images that illustrate the story
[*] Unique gameplay system that allows you to develop your personality and mitigate your weaknesses by using the Neural capacity resource. 
[*] Immersive soundtrack produced exclusively for the Robot’s Fate: Alice with over [b]20 musical tracks[/b]
[/list]

[h3]Cool features[/h3]
[list]
[*] Every choice you make affects Alice’s stats and unlocks unique perks.
[*] Shape Alice’s character to fit your playstyle with decisions that matter.
[*] Three different story paths lead to multiple endings.
[/list]

[i][b]You can have a look at Chapter 1 of Robot's Fate: Alice very soon - on August 19th, by playing our free DEMO.[/b][/i]

[h2][b][i]Wishlist the game now[/i],[/b] to get notified when the Demo comes out![/h2]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3091030

More news and updates will follow soon.

Ready to embark on this adventure? [i]Wishlist Robot's Fate:[/i] Alice on Steam now and stay tuned for more updates!
